newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech blue chips rebound slightly, PX50 off 0.1 pt.
newsitem.headline: Czech blue chips rebound slightly, PX50 off 0.1 pt.

text.p: Several Czech blue chips rallied in late trading on the Prague Stock Exchange on Monday, helping the bourse overcome fears of the economic damage incurred from heavy flooding in the eastern part of the country.
The PSE's three largest issues all lost ground at the daily fixing, but SPT Telecom, CEZ and Komercni Banka made late gains to finish slightly higher or unchanged.
The PX50 index, down 1.5 points at the fixing, closed off 0.1 point at 502.4.

Analysts said investor sentiment, weak to begin with, has fallen even further given estimates that damage from heavy flooding recently may total as much as 100 billion crowns, and could cost the already sluggish economy up to one full percentage point in GDP growth this year.

The floods covering low-lying areas of the eastern third of the Czech Republic -- as well as parts of Poland, Austria and Slovakia -- have forced tens of thousands from their homes, and closed several major industrial concerns.
Among the larger firms affected are tyre maker Barum Continental and Skoda Automobilova, both of which are major exporters.

Analysts said it may take three months for some firms to be back up and running at full capacity, biting hard into their bottom lines and giving already finicky investors yet another reason to avoid Czech equities.

"There are still no firm estimates of the flood damage, but I think the market feels the costs will be quite high. Given this, some construction and materials issues may benefit, but the overall outlook is a little pessimistic," said one foreign dealer.

Torrential rains helped push water levels last week to their highest in more than a century, flooding nearly one-third of the country and forcing several major firms, and hundreds of medium-sized ones to halt or reduce output.
Flooding still remains a major factor in much of the eastern and southeastern areas.
